GA-SEC-001.cause: GhostAttach found a fallback driver for this device, but the driver is not signed/verified. Policy rule 3 blocked it.
GA-SEC-001.action: Do NOT force-load the driver. Obtain a verified build of it (or sign it through the future update channel), then reboot.

GA-DRV-101.cause: No verified driver exists for this device, and no safe fallback was available. The device is disabled.
GA-DRV-101.action: The device stays off - that is the safe state. Add a verified driver to the registry in a future update.

GA-DRV-201.cause: A verified driver tried to attach but failed its probe. The device was quarantined (isolated) to prevent boot loops.
GA-DRV-201.action: Check device/driver compatibility. The quarantine is correct behavior - lift it only after fixing the driver.

KBD-001.cause: The PS/2 keyboard controller did not respond to the boot probe. The interactive shell has no input.
KBD-001.action: Check the emulator's input configuration (PS/2 device present?). On real hardware: check the controller.

EXP-001.cause: Log export was requested but the COM1 UART failed its loopback self-test at boot.
EXP-001.action: Check the emulator's -serial flag. Without serial, use the on-screen logs-ai output instead.

TEST-PANIC-001.cause: A deliberate test panic was requested via the panic-test shell command. This is an exercise, not a real failure.
TEST-PANIC-001.action: None needed. Reboot the VM. If you did NOT run panic-test, treat this as a real incident and investigate who did.

REC-BLOCK-999.cause: Someone (or the boot self-check) attempted a high-risk or irreversible recovery action. The policy gate refused it.
REC-BLOCK-999.action: None - the block is correct and unconditional. If you need this capability, it must arrive as a verified, signed, reversible action in a future catalog, never as an override.

REC-ACT-004.cause: A recovery action passed approval but its apply step failed. State was left unchanged.
REC-ACT-004.action: Report this as a RecoveryEngine bug; include the log.

PKG-SUG-001.cause: A verified manifest matches the currently active module version, so the package is available for the human-driven approve/apply/verify flow.
PKG-SUG-001.action: Review package details inside KamikazeOS, then run approve-pkg/apply-pkg/verify-pkg only if you accept the risk.

PKG-BLOCK-001.cause: A recovery package failed the deterministic verification chain: unsigned, invalid, unknown trust anchor, high-risk, irreversible, checksum mismatch, or blocked payload type.
PKG-BLOCK-001.action: Do not override the block. Use only a future verified, reversible manifest that passes the trust-anchor policy.

PKG-ACT-001.cause: A human approved a package that passed the manifest and policy checks.
PKG-ACT-001.action: Continue with apply-pkg, then verify-pkg. Approval alone does not change module state.

PKG-ACT-002.cause: The package switched metadata to the inactive A/B module slot and marked it pending verification.
PKG-ACT-002.action: Run verify-pkg before trusting the new slot. Use rollback-pkg if verification fails or confidence drops.

PKG-ACT-003.cause: Post-apply verification passed: expected slot, expected version, no new criticals, and acceptable health delta.
PKG-ACT-003.action: No immediate action required. rollback-pkg remains the manual escape hatch while rollback metadata exists.

PKG-ACT-004.cause: Post-apply verification failed after a package apply.
PKG-ACT-004.action: Run rollback-pkg for the failed package to return to the known-good slot.

PKG-PENDING-VERIFY.cause: A package was applied before a reboot or crash and its new slot has not been verified yet.
PKG-PENDING-VERIFY.action: Run verify-pkg for the applied package, or rollback-pkg to return to the known-good slot.

PKG-RB-001.cause: A package rollback switched active module metadata back to the recorded known-good slot.
PKG-RB-001.action: Confirm health on the next boot and investigate why the new slot was not kept.

MAN-000.cause: Package manifests were loaded from disk sectors and checked against the simulated trust-anchor policy.
MAN-000.action: No action needed unless a specific package is blocked.

MAN-001.cause: No valid disk manifests were present, so KamikazeOS fell back to the built-in seed manifest set.
MAN-001.action: Run seed-manifests confirm inside KamikazeOS if you want the seed manifests persisted to disk.

MAN-002.cause: The built-in seed manifest set was written to the manifest sectors.
MAN-002.action: No action needed. Future boots should report disk-sourced manifests.

PST-000.cause: Persistent package lifecycle state was restored from disk.
PST-000.action: No action needed. Package status now survives QEMU restarts.

PST-100.cause: A human reset package lifecycle state and A/B slot metadata.
PST-100.action: Review packages and slots after reboot; journal history was preserved.

SLOT-000.cause: Module A/B slot metadata was restored from disk and now defines the running module versions.
SLOT-000.action: No action needed unless a slot is pending verification.

BOOT-001.cause: The kernel was started by something that is not a Multiboot-compliant loader; boot information is untrusted.
BOOT-001.action: Boot via GRUB or QEMU's -kernel option.
